slide.text: The FCT can phase implementation without losing control
The platform supports a phased rollout that starts with land-administration urgency and then extends into geospatial review, field continuity, AI-assisted throughput, and executive oversight.

text.p: Deploy parcel records, title-flow visibility, role-based queues, and signed audit control for core FCT land-administration workflows.
Expand into desk-based map review, parcel overlays, mass-housing and area-council regularisation visibility, and exception monitoring.
Add low-connectivity missions, evidence continuity, and AI-assisted intake to reduce friction and improve processing discipline.
Layer in broader revenue visibility, supervisory digests, public verification controls, and expansion into wider federal or agency-linked workflows.

slide.text: This phased path lets the FCT start with title continuity and oversight priorities while preserving a credible route to deeper geospatial and governance modernization.
The platform can begin where public risk is highest and expand without replacing the underlying operational backbone.
